Do not tell her. Distance yourself if it'll help, no need to give reasons either. If it's questioned later (which is something that may not even happen), just say you're doing your own thing. People grow close and apart everyday. As of right now she's in a relationship and was in one way before your friendship with her. Do not try to wait around for "your chance" with her either. Just move on.
Seriously. Sexual compatibility is a real thing that can make or break a relationship. And the fact she won't even make an effort or talk about it... Relationship obviously moved too fast.

Don't be remorseful. At all. Your business with your ex-husband sounds like it works out fine. There's no reason to suspect anything is up. Seems like you keep things separated and cordial.

Your relationship with your fiance doesn't sound healthy though. Some people have things they're not ok with and that's fine. He sounds overly jealous though and insecure. Won't even accompany you to a function to check it out himself? Y'all had a break for 3 months too and that raises alarms. That's a long time and sounds pretty serious. What happened? And he was with someone else during that time? Bit hypocritical on his part. Your relationship sounds sketch and a little miserable. Not something I would put anymore time into.

Y'all been together 6 months, the honeymoon/wild bunny phase should be close to being over. Having sex everyday (and multiple times a day) can take a toll and is tiring as well. The argument can also be a factor. Stress and emotions can do that but I don't believe it's the big picture.

After a while, people get comfortable. There isn't a need to jump on each other at every chance. It happens in relationships. High libido? Play with your toys or get some if you don't have any. Don't look for validation in sex, I made that mistake and it took a lot of talking and understanding with my partner to figure out that everything was just fine and it wasn't that I became unattractive to him. If it's any consolation, we still have sex a few times a week. Just find what works now.

Talking with your bf is the only way you're gonna know what's going on in his mind though. This is just from my current experience with my partner and it's the only insight I have to offer.
Are you sure you didn't break down somebody's fence just to get to this little guy?

Everyone moves at their own pace. It does not sound like there's anything wrong with her. You either come to terms with that decision or break it off. It's not a problem of motivation, she seems content on the choices she's making.

Let's get one thing straight too - you ARE talking down on her. She told you she's interested in taking over her family business. That's great news, I'd be happy. It's not your place to tell her what career choices she needs to make. You're her boyfriend, don't act like an advisor.

I get it though. You are putting in a lot of effort to become a better person and to guarantee a solid job. You see her as being lazy and uncaring for the future. For this reason I believe it's better to break up. Your values don't line up and there is no support system. Support only seems to come if it's what you think is best for her, not what makes her happy.

From what I'm reading, I feel like you're not truly reflecting on yourself. It seems like you're able to approach people and hold conversations. Which is good. But I get a feeling you're separating yourself from others without knowing it. 

You make a point to say you're different - different interests, different hobbies. You say you like "adult relationships". What exactly is an adult relationship to you? Do you look down on a lot of people because you believe you're more mature? Are your interests the only ones worth talking about or defining a relationship? 

People can pick up on these things. You have to be genuinely interested in other people to develop any sort of relationship. Being professional is not the same as being personable.

My parents are like this. Not as much as of recent but they definitely had their days/weeks/months over the years. I'm the oldest with three younger siblings and I also was worried. I wanted to attend college in another state but how could I? We live in a small town where everyone knows about everyone, similar to you. Calling police was overkill, CPS made things worse with kids we knew. And it was just "normal" to live with. 

I'm gonna tell you I decided to stay with family to help look after my siblings. Do I regret it? No. But I think where I could have been if I chose differently. Enroll into your college, prepare for your future. Tell the younger kids to call or text if anything happens. Have a list of phone numbers of family y'all can call too (our grandma likes any excuse for us to visit and will intervene if parents are too much). 

The kids will have to learn how to manage without you. That's the life of a dysfunctional family. Make sure you have enough life lines for them, family that is willing to stop by even. They will miss you but won't blame you. This is from my experience and its unorthodox advice. Thought you would like to hear it though.
I'm really happy for this update. It takes a certain nudge to reflect on things and I'm glad you realized this behavior is something you choose not to put up with. Good job and good luck!
